newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower, March leads the way.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower, March leads the way.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended lower Monday in a retreat from last week's rally to three-week highs, as speculators and producer countries took profits on the recent run-up.

Dealers said an absence of follow-through buying following Friday's 27-point leap quickly dampened sentiment this morning. After gapping down 0.07 cent, most-active March slumped to 0.20 cent below the previous close.
Persistent selling by a U.S. trade house also hurt the nearby contract, brokers said.
But after the early downturn, the market barely budged for the second-half of the session, and bargain hunting by other industry operators provided a buffer at the lows.
Benchmark March delivery fell 0.17 cent a lb on the day, to 10.56 cents, having ranged from 10.53 to 10.66. Second-position May eased 0.15, to 10.64, while the outer months ended off 0.11 cent.
An estimated 11,233 lots were exchanged on the day, with the bulk of the turnover posted early on.
Technically, the market staved off a test of support for the time being, but traders said the market was liable to test key downside levels in the next several days.
"If you get some closes under 10.50 cents you might see some new selling come into the market," said one. Strong resistance was eyed in the 10.75-10.80 range.
